title: Fine meadow variants
notes: Several actual hexes of open olive meadow. Compare the irregular yellow-green blades, bare-earth flecks, sparse stones and small shrubs.

title: Stony meadow variants
notes: Concentrated scree below the northern crater, dispersed eastern stones and larger southern rock scatter. These are separate samples of the same ground family.

title: Dense woodland and scalloped edge
notes: A connected western woodland patch with tightly overlapping crowns and irregular grass openings along its eastern edge. Bright small canopy lobes sit above dark contacts.

title: Open woodland and a detached copse
notes: Northern trees thin into winding meadow corridors. The detached copse at r08c05 provides a smaller complete foliage silhouette for comparison.

title: Complete northern crater and disturbed ground
notes: The crater is centred on r12c03 but its raised rim and disturbed apron extend into neighbouring hexes. Keep this connected group when studying the complete shape.

title: Southern paired craters
notes: Two differently sized depressions share disturbed earth. The larger crater sits around r40c04; the elongated smaller crater crosses r41c05 and neighbouring cells.

title: Two small rocky knolls
notes: Two separate complete small rises: the pale shoulder beside the central road and the sharper eastern crest. Each includes neighbouring hexes containing its grassy slopes and scrub.

title: Broad western grassy hill
notes: A complete broad hill above the southern road. Multiple hexes retain the rocky crest, bright ridges, grassy shoulders and deep planted gullies.

title: Northern huts and ancillary objects
notes: Both detached huts, their small accompanying boxes and shadows. The white circular symbol beside the lower hut is an interface marker; it is retained as source context.

title: Northern paved-road junction
notes: The connected branching asphalt junction and its approaches. Lane markings, pale edges and warm gravel shoulders cross the real hex boundaries.

title: Diagonal road turning toward the central base
notes: A connected road sequence preserves the diagonal approach, curved transition and north-south segment. The white bar near the base is an entrance feature rather than a water bridge.

title: Winding earth track through meadow
notes: Connected hexes follow the narrow track southwest from the central base, through its near-vertical section and down to the paved-road junction. Pale ruts and a darker grassy centre remain visible.

title: Complete lake, rocky shore and exposed water rocks
notes: The connected lake group retains its irregular shore, open teal water and four exposed rocks. The water rocks cross the r28-r30 cells; shoreline pieces are included around the perimeter.

title: Creek bend and asymmetric rocky banks
notes: Connected creek cells south of the lake show the narrow channel, pale bank rocks, grass projections and bordering woodland. The long bridge is included where it crosses the channel.

title: Short bridge at the lake outlet
notes: The diagonal deck lies chiefly in r33c07. Its neighbouring cells preserve both abutments, the rocky outlet banks and the path approaching from the west.

title: Complete north-south creek bridge
notes: The pale longitudinal deck is centred on r37c07 and extends toward r39c07. Adjacent cells retain the shore contacts and channel on both sides of the crossing.

title: Complete northern headquarters compound
notes: Keep the complete connected multihex installation: four bright metallic corner assemblies, connecting members, both red entrance roofs and the central passage. The surrounding river and road remain context.

title: Complete southern headquarters compound
notes: A second complete example of the headquarters family spans several true cells. Include all four corner assemblies, the connecting perimeter and red gate roofs; the red lower-boundary interface tabs are excluded.

title: Complete central service base
notes: The connected group preserves the emblem building, western red-accent shed, small huts, eastern white framed equipment, fencing and entrance. Equipment identities are visually ambiguous.

title: Complete southwestern service base
notes: The repeated service installation is retained as a complete connected group, including the main building, red-accent shed, white equipment, fencing and paved entrance.
